title: Supply and customer demand in 4-player games: measure first, then propose one fix
problem: Informal feedback (REP-045): "supply cant keep up with demand" from mid-game and players ended up with nothing to buy. By code: no lorry comes on Market Days (days 3, 6, 9, 12; game.ts), and 4 shops add 1 of each fruit (about 17 fruits on a lorry day against a buying capacity of 16 for four shops). This is a hypothesis; no one has measured it. Owner (same message): "feels like theres too much customer towards the final few turns". By code, walk-ins per day are players minus 2 in the first half and players minus 1 in the second half, plus 1 on a Market Day, and unserved customers wait one more day; so late days have more customers.
scope: Step 1, no game change: simulate 2, 3 and 4 shop games and measure, per day, how much of each fruit is on the market before each shop buys, how often a shop finds the fruit it wants gone, and how this differs on Market Days; and measure demand the same way: customers and fruit wanted per day, how much of it is served, and how the last few days compare with the early days
Step 2: propose one change with options and same-seed before and after results (candidates: a smaller delivery on Market Days, or more supply for 4 shops); the owner picks
Step 3, after the owner picks: implement, bump RULES_VERSION, update RULES.md and data, run the checks
Any change must be playable by hand with cards (DEC-027)
The proposal in step 2 may change supply, demand, or both; the owner picks
exclusions: Changing customers, prices, specialities or computer players

acceptance.text: Measurement report shows supply and customer demand per day for 2, 3 and 4 shops, with sample size, including the last three days against the first three
acceptance.evidence: REP-049 (2026-10-27 23:16): 2, 3 and 4 shops, 300 games each, all Normal computers; what-ifs 200 games; first 3 days against last 3 days; computer players only.

acceptance.text: Owner sets a target (for example, the largest share of shop turns that may find nothing to buy) before any change is chosen
After the change: same-seed comparison meets the owner target; verify and verify:full pass
A human playtest of the changed rules (not computer only) is recorded or explicitly deferred by the owner
